s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal pain with anemia and hemodynamic stability, with a history of hypervascular liver lesions
salient_findings: Anemia with hemoglobin level of 4.4 mmol/L
Subcapsular hepatic bleeding on abdominal ultrasound
Active bleeding from a hypervascular liver lesion on contrast-enhanced CT
key_facts: 64-year-old white man
Admitted in March 2016
On therapeutic anticoagulation for paroxysmal pre-shimmering
History of two hypervascular liver lesions in segment IV
Biopsies in August 2015 showed histologically proven adenoma without malignancy
Hemodynamically stable on presentation
No weight loss, fever, or constitutional symptoms
Normal α-fetoprotein, carcinoembryonic antigen, and carbohydrate antigen 19-9 levels
Abdominal ultrasound revealed subcapsular hepatic bleeding
Contrast-enhanced CT confirmed active bleeding from one of the two hypervascular lesions
Angiographic embolization and conservative management resolved bleeding
Follow-up CT in April 2016 showed persistent hypervascular lesions

shortlist.label: Liver adenoma
shortlist.why_kept: History of biopsies showing histologically proven adenoma without malignancy

shortlist.label: Inflammatory hepatocellular adenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Hypervascular lesions and history of adenoma

shortlist.label: Hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Hypervascular lesions, although less likely given the clinical context

raw.rationale: The patient had biopsies in August 2015 that showed histologically proven adenoma without malignancy, and the presentation of acute-onset abdominal pain and anemia due to bleeding from one of the hypervascular lesions is consistent with a complication of liver adenoma, particularly given the lack of weight loss, fever, or constitutional symptoms and normal tumor markers.

rejected.label: Hepatocellular carcinoma
rejected.why: Normal tumor markers and lack of typical features on imaging make this less likely

rejected.label: Telangiectatic adenoma
rejected.why: Not directly supported by the provided biopsy results or clinical presentation

rejected.label: Inflammatory hepatocellular adenoma
rejected.why: No specific evidence of inflammation or characteristic findings on imaging

rejected.label: Hemangioma
rejected.why: The lesions are described as hypervascular, which is more characteristic of adenomas, and hemangiomas typically do not bleed spontaneously
